title: Creating a Root Component knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Creating a Root Component”?
options: Creating a Root Component helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Creating a Root Component means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Creating a Root Component removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Creating a Root Component should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Creating a Root Component helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Creating a Root Component is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Root component responsibilities” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Root component responsibilities” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Root component responsibilities” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Root component responsibilities” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Root component responsibilities” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Root component responsibilities” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Root component responsibilities” under Creating a Root Component. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Creating a Root Component”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
